title: feat: add OpenAI fallbacks for GPT Image
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds hidden OpenAI direct fallback routes for `gptimage`, `gptimage-large`, and `gpt-image-2` while preserving their public IDs, aliases, pricing, access, and Azure primary routes.
- Falls back only when an OpenAI-branded Azure route returns 429; ambiguous timeouts and generic 5xx responses remain terminal to avoid duplicate generation and provider billing.
- Keeps Azure endpoint rotation isolated per model and skips a redundant per-user rate-limit check on the internal OpenAI fallback route.
- Adds a 6 RPM per-user token bucket for `gpt-image-2` only, based on seven days of production traffic (p95: 4 requests/user/minute).
- Verifies live OpenAI generation/editing and tests registry routing, provider request shapes, fallback observability/billing, timeout safety, regional rotation, and rate limiting.

gist.headline: The image hive has backups
gist.blurb: GPT Image now has a second pollinator waiting behind the Azure gate. When an OpenAI-branded Azure route is busy, the request can keep flying instead of circling the same flower.
gist.summary: Added hidden direct OpenAI fallback routes for gptimage, gptimage-large, and gpt-image-2 that activate only after an OpenAI-branded Azure route returns 429, while preserving public model IDs, aliases, pricing, access rules, and Azure-first routing.
gist.impact: Image requests for these GPT Image models can continue through OpenAI during Azure 429 congestion, while timeouts and generic 5xx responses remain safely terminal to prevent duplicate generations and billing; gpt-image-2 also now has a 6 RPM per-user limit.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy image-generation garden has three labeled seed packets—gptimage, gptimage-large, and gpt-image-2—feeding into an Azure-blue primary watering pipe, with a tucked-away OpenAI backup pipe opening only when a tiny 429 traffic sign appears. Polli should be a warm, observant garden mechanic using a small wrench to guide a single image request safely through the alternate pipe, surrounded by blooming code-plants and a gently glowing retro terminal.
